title: Privacy & cookies
html:
Privacy & cookies

Updated October 27, 2026

Your cookie choices

Essential cookies remember your choice and keep private admin access secure. Optional first-party analytics stays off until you accept it. Choose Essential only, Accept analytics, or Customize in the banner. You can reopen Cookie settings in the footer and withdraw permission at any time. Declining does not prevent you from reading the website.

Optional first-party analytics

When you accept, the site measures page views, published blog views, estimated browser visitors and visits. It records a public page path without query strings or URL fragments, a broad screen-size category, an optional external referrer domain without its path or search terms, a UTC event time, and pseudonymous browser/visit identifiers transformed with a server-side keyed hash. It does not store raw IP addresses, email addresses, full referrer URLs, raw user-agent strings, fingerprints, or session recordings in its analytics tables. No third-party analytics script is added by this feature.

Analytics is skipped for signed-in admins, known bots, and browsers sending Global Privacy Control or Do Not Track signals. Counts include only measured, consenting browsers and are estimates rather than an exact count of people.

Cookie durations

  • Cookie preference: up to 180 days. This necessary cookie remembers your choice.
  • Analytics browser identifier: up to 30 days, only after acceptance.
  • Analytics visit identifier: 30 minutes of inactivity, refreshed on measured page views, only after acceptance.
  • Private owner session: up to eight hours, with a 30-minute inactivity timeout. This is used only for admin sign-in.

Cookies are first-party, HttpOnly and Secure on production HTTPS. Withdrawing analytics permission deletes the browser and visit identifier cookies and stops future analytics. Previously recorded events are not automatically deleted by changing the cookie preference.

Storage and retention

Analytics records are stored in the publisher’s MySQL database and are available only in the authenticated admin dashboard as aggregate reports. Records older than 90 days are pruned during collection and dashboard access. The publisher should also schedule the supplied daily cleanup so deletion continues during quiet periods. Hashes and cookie expiry reduce direct identification, but this is pseudonymous data rather than guaranteed anonymous data.

Private administration and content

The owner signs in with a private email and password verified against a salted scrypt hash. Revocable, signed session cookies, origin checks and rate limits protect admin access. There is no public registration. Posts, categories and images are stored in MySQL; draft articles and unpublished uploaded images require owner access. Owner activity records contain publishing actions and article identifiers.

Hosting and security logs

The hosting provider may process request information, including IP addresses and browser details, to deliver and secure the site. Hosting/security logs are separate from optional page-view analytics and are not disabled by the analytics choice. The publisher must review the hosting provider’s settings and retention separately.

Comments, advertising and other services

Public comment submission is disabled. Historical comments remain available to the owner for moderation. This feature does not install advertising trackers, Google Analytics or session replay. If other services are introduced, the publisher must review the disclosures and consent controls before enabling them.

Contact

The publisher still needs to supply a public privacy contact. Review this notice against the final services and retention settings before launch. Do not submit passwords, API keys or sensitive personal data in public posts or comments.
